subject: Polity
topic: Directive Principles of State Policy — mixed tiers
description: Part IV, Articles 36-51, classifications, key articles, 42nd amendment additions

questions.stem: Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: DPSP — Part IV, Articles 36-51. Part III (12-35) — Fundamental Rights. Part IVA (Article 51A) — Fundamental Duties (added by 42nd Amendment, 1976; 11 duties after 86th Amendment added the right to education-linked duty in 2002). DPSP are non-justiciable (Article 37 — not enforceable by any court), but 'fundamental in the governance of the country' and the State has a duty to apply them while making laws.

questions.stem: DPSP in the Indian Constitution is BORROWED FROM the constitution of:

options.option_text: Ireland (which itself borrowed it from the Spanish Constitution)

questions.explanation: DPSP — borrowed from Ireland (Irish Constitution of 1937). Other borrowings: Parliamentary system + rule of law (UK); FRs + judicial review + Preamble structure (US); Federal scheme + residuary powers with centre (Canada); Concurrent List (Australia); Emergency provisions (Germany — Weimar); Procedure for amendment (South Africa); Five-Year Plans (USSR); Fundamental Duties (USSR). Ireland adopted the concept from the Spanish Constitution, originally a Spanish innovation.

questions.stem: Article 44 of the Constitution directs the State to secure for citizens a:

options.option_text: Uniform Civil Code throughout the territory of India

questions.explanation: Article 44 — Uniform Civil Code (UCC). Currently civil matters (marriage, divorce, succession, adoption) follow personal laws by religion. Goa is the only state with a UCC (inherited from Portuguese colonial code). Uttarakhand became the first state to legislate a UCC in 2024. Article 39A — equal justice + free legal aid. Article 41 — right to work, education, public assistance. Article 43 — living wage. Shah Bano case (1985) and Shayara Bano case (2017, triple talaq) revived UCC debate.

questions.stem: Articles 39(b) and 39(c), which direct ownership and control of material resources to subserve the common good, are classified as:
questions.explanation: DPSP classification (academic, not constitutional): SOCIALIST — Articles 38, 39, 39A, 41, 42, 43, 43A, 47 (welfare state, equitable distribution). GANDHIAN — Articles 40 (village panchayats), 43 (cottage industries), 43B (cooperatives), 46 (SC/ST/weaker sections), 47 (prohibition), 48 (cow protection). LIBERAL-INTELLECTUAL — Articles 44 (UCC), 45 (early childhood care), 48 (modern agriculture), 49 (monuments), 50 (separation of judiciary from executive), 51 (international peace). 39(b)/(c) shielded from FR challenge by Article 31C (added by 25th Amendment, 1971).

questions.stem: Article 48A — protection and improvement of environment, forests and wildlife — was added to the Constitution by the:
questions.explanation: 42nd Amendment, 1976 ('Mini-Constitution', Indira Gandhi's emergency-era amendment) — added FOUR new DPSP: Article 39A (equal justice + free legal aid); 43A (workers' participation in management); 48A (environment, forests, wildlife); also created Part IVA (Fundamental Duties — Article 51A, 10 duties). 86th Amendment, 2002 — modified Article 45 (childhood care below 6) and added Article 21A (Right to Education as FR). 97th Amendment, 2011 — added 'cooperative societies' (43B) and Part IXB. Note — DPSP have grown over time.

questions.stem: Which DPSP article directs the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government?
questions.explanation: Article 40 — village panchayats as units of self-government (Gandhian principle). Translated into reality by 73rd Amendment (1992) — added Part IX + Schedule 11; mandated panchayati raj institutions, gram sabhas, reservations for SC/ST/women (1/3, raised to 1/2 in many states). Article 50 — separation of judiciary from executive (achieved by Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973). Article 45 — early childhood care (originally free + compulsory primary education, now covered by Article 21A). Article 39 — distribution of material resources.

questions.stem: Regarding the relationship between Fundamental Rights (FRs) and DPSP, which is CORRECT?

options.option_text: DPSP are subordinate to FRs but Article 31C (since 1971) gives some DPSP precedence over Articles 14, 19
DPSP are enforceable in court like FRs

questions.explanation: Champakam Dorairajan (1951) — FRs prevail over DPSP. State of Kerala v. N.M. Thomas — courts try to harmonise. 25th Amendment (1971) added Article 31C — laws giving effect to 39(b)/39(c) cannot be challenged on grounds of Article 14 or 19. 42nd Amendment tried to extend this to ALL DPSP, but Minerva Mills (1980) struck down that extension — basic-structure doctrine: harmony between FRs and DPSP is part of the basic structure. So FRs and DPSP are now read complementarily; courts interpret FRs in light of DPSP (e.g., environmental rights derived from Article 21 + 48A).
